errands.label: Weekly groceries
errands.reads: A repeatable basket of ordinary staples, with enough flexibility for price, nutrition, and household habit.

steps.note: A staple the household will actually finish.
Milk for breakfast, coffee, or cooking.
Low-cost protein that can carry more than one meal.
Vegetables that will still be there later in the week.
A reliable base for the night dinner needs to be fast.
A backup sauce for the meal that turns pasta-shaped.

errands.label: Breakfast reset
errands.reads: A low-drama breakfast shelf that keeps mornings easy without letting sugar or packaging make every choice.

steps.note: A plain base for slow mornings or fast ones.
An easy cereal for mornings that do not leave time.
Milk that works with cereal, oats, or coffee.
A spoonable breakfast or snack when cooking is not happening.
A small sweet thing where sugar and sourcing still matter.
The morning drink, if coffee is part of the house.

errands.label: Pick a bank
errands.reads: Choose where everyday money should sit, with fees, fossil exposure, access, and transparency visible together.

steps.note: The everyday account where pay, bills, and savings begin.

errands.label: Move your subscriptions
errands.reads: A calm pass over recurring media and service spending, keeping what is worth paying for and replacing what is not.

steps.note: Music access that fits how you listen and how artists get paid.
Reading access that does not trap every book in one account.
News worth paying attention to, and sometimes worth paying for.
Recurring tools to keep, replace, or cancel with intent.

errands.label: De-Google
errands.reads: Replace the most important Google-shaped dependencies first, without pretending every swap has to happen in one weekend.

steps.note: Pick the search, email, maps, notes, or storage habit to move first.
Set a password home before moving accounts around.
Choose a phone path if the operating system is part of the lock-in.
Pick an assistant without rebuilding the old dependency.

errands.label: New phone, sanely
errands.reads: Pick a phone path around longevity, repair, privacy, and the possibility that not buying new is the best move.

steps.note: Choose the phone, refurbished route, or keep-it-longer route.
Set up passwords and authentication before migration day.
Move default apps and services with care.

errands.label: Clean the bathroom cabinet
errands.reads: Restock the small daily products that touch skin and water, while cutting duplicate bottles and vague clean-beauty claims.

steps.note: The daily item most homes run out of first.
Hand or bath soap that gets used every day.
Body wash only if a bar is not the right fit.
Shampoo you will use enough to justify the bottle.
Deodorant for ordinary days, not a shelf of maybes.
A shaving setup with less repeat waste.
Period care that fits body, budget, and access.

errands.label: Dinner for 8
errands.reads: A crowd meal that is filling, flexible, and values-aware without making the host solve every food system problem.

steps.note: A large-batch base that keeps the table fed.
Protein that scales without much cost.
Vegetables for volume, color, and fewer last-minute trips.
Sauce if the meal turns pasta-shaped.
A simple dressing if greens join the table.
A small dessert with the cocoa question visible.

errands.label: Gift under 20
errands.reads: Find a modest gift that still has a story, a use, or a better ownership trail than panic-buying.

steps.note: A book, ebook, or reading route that can travel with the person.
A treat where cocoa sourcing is part of the choice.
Coffee if the gift is a morning ritual.
Tea if the gift is a calmer ritual.
A donation route when the best gift is not another object.

errands.label: Back to school
errands.reads: A school-year setup around learning access, repairable devices, safer accounts, and fewer one-season purchases.

steps.note: The subjects or skills this term will actually ask of you.
Reading access before buying every text new.
A computer only if a device is truly needed.
Account safety before the year fills with logins.
Paper basics for the places digital still does not fit.

errands.label: First apartment
errands.reads: A first practical home kit for cleaning, dishes, laundry, paper, and a few daily-care basics.

steps.note: Clean the surfaces you have before buying a cupboard of extras.
Dish soap for the sink you will use every day.
Detergent that fits the machine and skin in the house.
Toilet paper, tissues, or towels without buying blind.
Hand soap for the bathroom or kitchen.
Toothpaste for the cabinet before the first rushed morning.

errands.label: Switch your search
errands.reads: Try a different search default long enough to learn the tradeoff between convenience, privacy, ads, and public knowledge.

steps.note: A search engine or search-shaped tool to try first.
A source-checking habit to pair with the new default.
